Chlorofluorocarbons or CFCs, maybe better known under DuPont brand name - Freon.

We were causing massive atmospheric damage with these starting with an increasingly large hole that was forming in the ozone layer of Antarctica. Humanity came together and every single member nation of the UN ratified the Montreal Protocol which phased these out of use worldwide. The ozone layer has managed to recover from nearly all of the damage we were causing with these.

Relevant anecdote from this as well. The main producer of these was DuPont. When governments looked to start rolling back and regulating against their usage DuPont began organizing such efforts as the "Alliance for Responsible CFC Policy" to try to frame such actions against CFCs as anti-science or anti-scientific. That was in 1978. In 1986 when DuPont had developed and patented a derivative that didn't cause environmental damage, they rapidly acknowledged the damage that CFCs were causing and joined the lobby for them to be banned worldwide.
